replies.author: cryptoman_101
replies.body:
A free demo proves the software can be tested, not that your claimed edge is real.

Your own MQL5 listing explicitly states that historical statistics do not guarantee future results. The listing also does not provide independently verified live results substantiating your claimed PF above 6 and 75 to 80% win rate after spreads, commissions, and slippage.

Show a verified live track record with a meaningful trade sample, maximum drawdown, average win versus average loss, and all trading costs included.

Until then, this is a marketing claim, not proof. **I asked for evidence, not a $699 checkout link.** 😂

replies.author: H_TRADING87
replies.body: # Oh, you’ve forgotten that you can download it for free and try it out! Tell me, would you pay for something without testing it first? Give it a try—test it over an extended period—and I challenge you to find any automated trading expert advisor that delivers results like these. We aren’t forcing you to buy anything; I’m simply suggesting that you try it. We are looking to build a reputation for our tools.

replies.author: cryptoman_101
replies.body:
You're missing the point, bud. Nobody said you're forcing anyone to buy anything.

According to MQL5's own rules, the free demo version of an EA can only be tested in the Strategy Tester. You cannot run it on a live chart to independently verify its live performance. And MQL5 explicitly states that passing its automated historical test does not guarantee future results. [Source: MQL5 Market rules](https://www.mql5.com/en/market/rules)

So your challenge lets me test historical performance, not independently verify the claim that this EA achieves a PF above 6 and a 75 to 80% win rate in live trading.

You originally claimed to have already done rigorous forward and backward testing on raw spread accounts. **Where is the independently verifiable forward track record?** Show the actual results, trade count, maximum drawdown, average win versus average loss, and trading costs.

"Try it yourself" is not evidence. And challenging people to find a better EA doesn't validate yours.

**You made the extraordinary claim. The burden of proof is on you, not on everyone else to disprove it.**

replies.author: H_TRADING87
replies.body:
**Fair point regarding the MQL5 Market demo restrictions—nobody is disputing how MetaQuotes limits demo builds to the Strategy Tester to protect underlying IP. However, confusing platform restrictions with a lack of real-world validation is where your assumption falls short.**

**Here is the breakdown of how the performance metrics were evaluated:**

1. **Forward Execution Metrics: The win rates (\~75–80%), profit factor (>6.0), and tight drawdown limits (sub-7%) were recorded through real-time forward execution on live MT5 raw-spread accounts under real market volatility—not just backtests.**
2. **Slippage & Spread Reality: Real trading requires accounting for live broker execution, variable spreads, and slippage on XAUUSD. The algorithm’s dual-engine framework (S1 Reversal / S2 Momentum) was built specifically to adapt to these conditions without repainting or lagging.**
3. **Data & Verification: Quantitative logic is proven through consistent trade logs, win/loss distributions, and execution consistency over significant trade samples. All performance parameters and logs exist to back up these claims.**

**Skepticism is healthy in algo-trading, but passing judgment without analyzing the actual algorithm logic or reviewing live trade logs isn't critical thinking—it's just speculation. Let the technical execution speak for itself.**

replies.author: cryptoman_101
replies.body:
You can't even reply on your own, using ChatGPT to create a reply that is not even addressing the issue I am talking about.

and thanks for confirming my point. You say the data and logs exist, but you still haven't presented independently verifiable evidence.

I'm not claiming your EA cannot work. I'm saying that a PF above 6, a 75 to 80% win rate, and less than 7% drawdown are extraordinary claims that deserve verifiable evidence. A public live account with a meaningful track record, showing the equity curve, trade history, drawdown, and trading costs, would be a much stronger case than a verbal assurance that the logs exist.

You keep asking me to test your product, but **testing whether a product works and verifying whether your advertised performance claims are true are two different things.**

You say you want to build a reputation? Excellent. Publish independently verifiable results and let the numbers speak.

Until then, you have made a performance claim, not demonstrated a proven trading edge. No amount of confidence or technical terminology changes that.

This is my last reply in this thread, Have a nice day.

replies.author: H_TRADING87
replies.body: "Verification happens where results matter—in actual live deployment, not in public internet forums. Good luck with your trading journey."

replies.body: **I understand your point of view. Extraordinary claims require a closed loop of data, and building proprietary systems—owned by the developer—serves to protect core intellectual property, while the scope of deployment remains restricted and closed. Thank you for this discussion.**
